definition: Editing an existing image from a natural-language instruction ("make it winter, keep everything else"), via instruction-tuned image-to-image models or inversion of the source image into the model's latent space.
details: Editing an existing image from a natural-language instruction ("make it winter, keep everything else"), via instruction-tuned image-to-image models or inversion of the source image into the model's latent space. The capability that moved image models from generators to editors.

explainer.lead: Instruction-guided image editing changes an existing image according to a natural-language instruction while keeping the rest intact. It is the capability that moved image models from generators to editors.

tiers.eli5: You give the picture a plain-language instruction, like 'make it winter but keep everything else', and the tool edits the photo to match.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply instruction-tuned image-to-image models, or invert the source image into the model's latent space, to make edits. A pitfall is preserving everything the instruction does not ask to change.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as editing an existing image from a natural-language instruction, via instruction-tuned image-to-image models or inversion of the source image into the model's latent space. The capability that moved image models from generators to editors.

explainer.example: A user submits a summer photo with the instruction 'make it winter, keep everything else', and the edited image shows snow while the people and layout stay the same.
